function: p. 1: Multi-agent DDQN multichannel assignment and DDPG power allocation at terrestrial gNBs that share LEO satellite spectrum, maximizing global satellite-terrestrial spectrum efficiency under user QoS constraints.
system: p. 12: LEO satellite (600 km) sharing 17.5 GHz, 200 MHz in N=10 channels with NOMA terrestrial gNBs (up to seven, p. 11); antennas modeled by gains only.
method: p. 10: Multi-agent reinforcement learning: DDQN with value decomposition for channel assignment, DDPG actor-critic for power; centralized training with distributed execution (CTDE) under a Dec-POMDP (p. 7).
data_channel: p. 12: Custom simulator: free-space loss with Shadowed-Rician fading (LEO links), Nakagami-m fading (terrestrial links), Gauss-Markov outdated CSI; channels randomly generated each time slot (p. 13); no dataset.
test_conditions: p. 14: Trained at N=10 channels, Km=16 users per gNB; tested at K=6, 8, 12, 16 users (Fig. 7); also Pmax 15-45 dBm and M=1-7 gNBs sweeps.
baselines: p. 13: Non-learned: exhaustive search with iterative power allocation, GD-FP (greedy channel, fractional programming power), random policy; learned: DQN-based joint channel and power allocation [30].
metrics: p. 13: Average episode reward; average and real-time spectrum efficiency (bps/Hz) versus power, user density and gNB count; execution time (p. 15).
complexity: p. 15: Table III execution times: DCSS 2.95e-3 s, DQN-based 9.22e-4 s, GD-FP 8.25e-2 s, exhaustive 8.123e3 s; complexity orders of both networks given on p. 11.
q1_support: p. 5: "Shadowed-Rician fading distribution" - custom simulator: Shadowed-Rician for LEO links and Nakagami-m for terrestrial links (p. 12 parameters); TR 38.811 [26] is cited only for elevation-angle geometry on p. 4, not as the channel model; no measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "densities K = {6, 8, 12, 16} using the trained DNNs model of" - models trained with N = 10 channels and Km = 16 users per gNB are tested with 6, 8 and 12 users per gNB (Fig. 7).
q3_support: p. 13: "higher than DRL-based joint allocation algorithm, 16.02%" - DCSS is 13.58% above the earlier DQN-based learned method [30], 16.02% above GD-FP, 64.18% above random policy and 5.5% below exhaustive search, all in spectrum efficiency.
q4_support: p. 15: "Table III illustrates the execution times of the trained models" - measured runtime of DCSS 2.950e-3 s versus 8.123e3 s for exhaustive search; p. 11: "computational complexity of channel assignment network" gives the order of complexity.
q5_support: p. 12: "are provided with Tensorflow 1.13 on Python 3.6 platform" - no code or data link; channels are simulated and no public dataset or measured data is used.
notes: Included, area 6: learned channel assignment and power allocation of terrestrial gNBs on links that share LEO satellite spectrum, with the satellite link rate in the objective; borderline above_phy because the agents sit at the terrestrial gNBs. q1=0: TR 38.811 [26] only supplies the elevation-angle geometry (p. 4). q2=1 rests only on the Fig. 7 test with other user densities (p. 14); Figs. 6 and 8 do not state retraining. [30] is an earlier DQN method for D2D channel and power control, applied here by the authors.
